newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich Insurance says bid succeeds for Protector.
newsitem.headline: Zurich Insurance says bid succeeds for Protector.

text.p: Zurich Insurance Co said its bid for Norwegian company Protector ASA had been successful, with binding offers of 97.6 percent of Protector share capital.
A Zurich statement said it expected to complete the take-over of protector in the first quarter of 1997.
Protector's board in September recommended shareholders sell out after Zurich offered 230 crowns per share, valuing the company at 550 million crowns or about 105 million Swiss francs.
"Zurich has received binding offers from shareholders representing a total of 97.6 percent of share capital," the Swiss insurer said.
"Pending regulatory approval, this percentage (of capital) allows us to take over the remaining 2.4 percent of shares under Norwegian law," Zurich said.
"Zurich expects to be able to complete the transaction in the first quarter of 1997," it added.
Zurich's offer was dependent on receiving at least 90 percent of Protector stock.
Protector is a specialist for international maritime insurance and energy business and for Norwegian industrial and commercial insurance. Gross premiums totaled 660 crowns in 1995.
Zurich said Protector was an ideal extension of its existing Norwegian business, which is mainly in personal and international business insurance.
